change_summary: Ran a second runtime-only C experiment by monkeypatching `signal_engine.strategy_c_earnings()` so otherwise-valid C signals were kept only when `features['avg_historical_surprise_pct'] >= 4.0`. Compared `A+B` versus magnitude-gated `A+B+C` across the same three non-overlapping windows. No repository code was left changed; only the experiment record and playbook were updated.

delta_metrics.note: Magnitude-aware surprise gating improved the C cohort itself, but it still failed to beat the A+B baseline in the primary window and contributed nothing in the two comparison windows because all C trades disappeared there.

hypothesis: If boolean surprise sign is too blunt for `earnings_event_long`, a magnitude-aware gate may work better: require `avg_historical_surprise_pct >= 4.0` so only stronger historical beaters can consume risk budget. If this captures genuine PEAD quality, gated `A+B+C` should beat `A+B` more stably than both the ungated stack and the sign-only gate.
next_retry_requires: Do not retry another single-field surprise-magnitude threshold as the sole C-revival mechanism
If C is revisited, the mechanism now needs either multi-field event scoring or explicit slot-interaction logic
Do not resume generic A/B micro-tuning while `LLM soft ranking` remains the highest-value conceptual direction and still blocked by replay coverage
notes: This matters because it falsifies the obvious 'use surprise magnitude instead of surprise sign' follow-up. The archive is no longer the excuse; the mechanism itself is too weak.

event_quality_gate.old: historical surprise magnitude only affects confidence indirectly via `positive_surprise_history`

rejection_reason: Rejected on Gate 4. A one-dimensional surprise-magnitude gate is still too sparse and too weak: it leaves a slightly less-bad C cohort in the primary window, but adds no edge in the other two windows and remains inferior to A+B overall.
